title: Sunny and the Cloud Shapes | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka lies in the grass and watches soft clouds drift across the moon, spotting a bunny, a leaf, and a wave in the shapes above. A dreamy bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
There were clouds tonight, but Sunny did not mind.

They were the soft kind — pale and slow, drifting across the face of the moon like thoughts drifting through a sleeping mind.

She lay down in a flat grassy clearing, looked straight up, and watched.

The first cloud was long and curved. Sunny tilted her head.

A bunny, she decided. A very fluffy cloud-bunny, hopping very slowly across the sky.

The bunny-cloud stretched. It changed. It became something else — a leaf, maybe. Or a wave. Sunny could not quite decide.

A new cloud drifted in from the west, rounder and softer. It covered the moon for just a moment, and the whole bush went a little dimmer, a little quieter. Then the moon emerged on the other side, brighter and clearer than before.

Sunny breathed in and out, in and out, watching the clouds come and go.

Every shape was different. Every shape became something new.

The stars peeked between clouds and then hid again, playing their own slow game.

Sunny's arms spread a little wider in the grass. Her breathing slowed. The clouds overhead kept moving — slow and soft and endless — and she kept watching.

Until she didn't.

Until her eyes closed and the clouds kept moving without her, gently, through the whole long night.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, clouds. Goodnight, little one.
